symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1754: `marketplace install` of a protected (add-on) module shipped as .mxmodule (Menditect MtaPluginModule 11.5.5, Marketplace 214717) failed with "file is not a database"; `mx module-import` refuses such a package outright ("Importing protected module is not supported", exit 111).
cause: The package's project.mpr is not an SQLite .mpr but one BSON document {_ProductVersion, Contents} holding the project as a single tree with every unit nested in its container, so every reader that expected SQLite failed and mx has no import for it.
file: cmd/mxcli/marketplace/moduletree.go (split the tree into units at Folders/Documents/DomainModel/ModuleSettings/ModuleSecurity of modules and folders; write them with AddRawUnit; write the declared package files beside the reference; refuse a tree newer than the project), cmd/mxcli/marketplace/scratch.go (PackageProject takes that path for a tree)
insight: Replacing `mx module-import` means replacing everything it does, not just the unit write: it also writes the package's declared files next to the .mpr and converts the module to the project's Mendix version. The first cut of mendixlabs/mxcli#1755 did only the units, which installs fine (install copies files from the .mpk) but gives `marketplace diff`/`update` a reference without javasource/javascriptsource — the #1441 'every action changed locally' failure again — and units in the package's schema. Ask which readers consume the reference (refcache.go isModelFile lists them), not only which writer produced it. The unit test asserts Start.java beside the reference, which only the InstallPackageFiles call writes; the conversion is not reproduced (no mx), only a newer tree is refused.
